articles.title: TC Energy closes First Nations investment deal for CGL pipeline
articles.description: TC Energy has announced the closing of an investment agreement that grants five Indigenous communities an economic interest in the Coastal GasLink (CGL) natural gas pipeline in British Columbia, Canada.

articles.description: ENGIE and shipping and logistics group CMA CGM have agreed a framework deal to jointly develop a large-scale biomethane production plant in Le Havre's industrial port zone in France.

articles.description: Shell, via its subsidiary Shell Petroleum, has reached an agreement to divest its entire interest in the Shell Nigeria Gas Group to Nigerian energy company Vaaris Energy.

articles.description: A limited fire erupted at Aramco's office complex in Dhahran and there were no casualties, Saudi authorities said.

articles.title: Aramco’s New Chinese JV Refinery Gets First Saudi Crude Cargo
articles.description: Saudi Aramco’s newest joint venture refinery in China has received its first cargo of Arab crude as it prepares for start-up, the Saudi oil giant said in a statement to Bloomberg on Wednesday, without providing a timeline for the start of commercial operations. Saudi Arabia and its state-owned oil giant early this decade embarked on a strategy to set up joint ventures with local Chinese partners to build refineries that would process Arab crude grades, to secure deliveries in China in the long term. articles.title: Oman Overtakes U.S. as India's Top LNG Supplier in September
articles.description: Oman was India’s single biggest LNG supplier in September, toppling the United States that held the top spot for months after the Iran war began, as European buyers are snapping up American cargoes and intensifying the competition of spot U.S. supply with Asia. The arbitrage economics have worked in Europe’s favor in recent weeks in attracting U.S. LNG cargoes, and European buyers gobbled up additional American supply amid historically low levels in gas storage sites across the EU ahead of the winter. As a result, India boosted imports…

articles.title: Trump Announces “Massive” Greenland Oil Exploration Plans
articles.description: “Massive” oil, gas, and minerals exploration will soon begin in Greenland, U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday, claiming that the territory has enormous resources of readily available oil. Last month, the United States, Denmark, and Greenland signed an agreement to strengthen defense and security in the Arctic and North Atlantic, easing months of tensions over President Trump’s frequent threats to seize the Danish territory. The agreement reaffirmed Danish sovereignty and the right to self-determination of Greenland…

articles.title: Saudi Aramco Headquarters Hit as Houthi Attacks Escalate
articles.description: Saudi Aramco’s administrative building in Dharan, eastern Saudi Arabia, was hit in attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis on Tuesday night and Wednesday morning, amid an escalation of the Saudi-Houthi standoff in recent days. Limited fire was reported at Aramco’s headquarters as Saudi Arabia continued to intercept and destroy missiles towards Dharan and the capital Riyadh. A ballistic missile launched by the Houthi militias toward Dhahran city was intercepted and destroyed, Major General Turki Al-Malki, Official Spokesperson…

articles.title: Taiwan Commits Up to $4.4 Billion to Alaska LNG Megaproject
articles.description: Taiwan has agreed to invest up to $4.4 billion in the Alaska LNG project and commit to buying 30% of its output over a period of 20 years, President Trump said, as quoted by AFP, during a campaign rally in Alaska. Earlier today, Taiwan confirmed its intention to spend over $4 billion on the Alaska LNG project and commit to buying liquefied gas from the new facility, which is yet to be built, along with a pipeline to carry the gas to the export terminal. articles.title: Rising Gasoline Prices Fuel Fresh Inflation Fears in the U.S.
articles.description: A surge in energy costs is expected to drive overall U.S. consumer inflation higher, with September numbers seen at 0.6% on a monthly basis by economists polled by Reuters. The official CPI data for September is due out later today. Gasoline prices in the United States went up by 7.1% last month, with the latest daily average national price at $4.3413 per gallon, according to AAA. This is close to what the average was a month ago, with the difference at $0.028 per gallon. Diesel prices, however, remain stubbornly high, at above $6 per gallon, although…

articles.title: Oil Prices Climb Above $106 as Iran Threatens More Tanker Attacks
articles.description: Crude oil prices moved higher earlier today, after Iranian officials told Reuters the country’s forces were planning to further intensify strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, deploying new tactics. Brent crude was trading at $106.37 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $94.72 per barrel, with the news that Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu had asked Trump to start bombing Iran again likely to also contribute to the price rise. articles.title: Saudis Tell OPEC That Oil Output Recovered from 3 Decade Low
articles.description: Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC that its crude production jumped by a third last month.

articles.title: Brent Steady Amid Middle East Tensions
articles.description: Oil prices settled mixed as Middle East supply threats persisted and traders took profits.

articles.title: Wall Street Sees Inflation Easing Even With Oil Above $90
articles.description: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) report is due to be released on Wednesday, with economists predicting that key inflation metrics continued to moderate in September despite elevated oil prices, giving the Fed room to slow down on interest rate hikes. For September, economists expect headline inflation growth to clock in at 0.5% month-over-month and 3.6%- 3.7% year-over-year, up from 0.4% m-o-m and 3.4% Y/Y in August. Meanwhile, core CPI, which excludes volatile energy and food prices, is seen climbing 0.2% in September, down from August’s…

articles.title: Record Tanker Rates Leave Heavy Crude Stranded in the Americas
articles.description: The Middle East crisis has driven tanker rates to all-time highs and created a shortage of vessels. This oil logistics problem is now causing a ripple effect, tipping the heavy crude market in North and South America into oversupply—while Asia and Europe grapple with a shortage of heavy grades. Canada is producing over 5 million barrels of crude daily, most of it heavy crude. Some 4 million barrels daily of that goes south to U.S. refineries. Venezuelan production has also moved higher after the U.S. disposed of the country’s government…

articles.title: Stranded Middle East LNG Supply Upends Gas Markets
articles.description: The LNG supply out of the Middle East has not recovered in any meaningful way seven and a half months after the Iran war choked oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Since March, some occasional LNG cargoes have managed to squeeze through the chokepoint where a fifth of global liquefied Natural Gas supplies passed before the war. The rare shipments are not making much of a difference in the global gas market, which suddenly found itself without a fifth of daily LNG supplies and whose second-largest producer, Qatar, is now barely moving…

articles.title: Asia to dominate global polyethylene capacity growth through 2030
articles.description: Growing consumption in packaging, construction, automotive, and consumer goods is driving polyethylene capacity additions across Asia.

articles.title: OPEC Sees Oil Demand Growth Surging to 2.6 Million Bpd in 2027
articles.description: OPEC just put a very large number on next year’s oil market: global demand growth of 2.6 million barrels per day in 2027, after growth of just 200,000 bpd this year. That would push average world oil demand from 105.7 million bpd in 2026 to 108.3 million bpd next year. OPEC also revised its 2027 demand forecast higher this month, even as it nudged this year’s growth estimate lower. Part of that jump has little to do with people suddenly driving a lot more. articles.title: Five Shale Stocks to Watch Before Third-Quarter Earnings
articles.description: Permian producers spent much of this year paying buyers to haul away the natural gas that comes up with their oil.
